# Rules and process fixes

## bm_store.py verify() problems at generation time

None. If a process fix belongs here anyway, it is one this session found some other way; write it in below.

## Notes (human, preserved verbatim on regeneration)

<!-- bm-human:begin -->
Four, each traceable to a mistake above.

**PF-1: the gate runs against a committed tree, never a dirty one.** Commit
first, then launch. A dirty tree makes `test_all.py` refuse green and list your
own edits as suite pollution, which costs a full run to discover. Mistake 1.

**PF-2: long gate runs carry `--artifacts DIR`.** The gate collapses a failing
suite to one line, so when `test_bm_handover.py` failed, its assertion text was
gone and recovering it cost a second run. The flag already existed. Use it.

**PF-3: a new tool is registered in FIVE places, and pyproject.toml is the one
that gets forgotten.** The full list, in the order the gate checks them:
`tools/test_all.py` SUITES, `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, `tools/bm_effects.py`
REGISTRY, `tools/write_sites.json`, and `pyproject.toml` py-modules. PO-6 says
open the file that READS a registry before adding to it; the corollary this
session learned is to enumerate ALL the readers first, because four out of five
is a failure. Mistake 2.

**PF-4: never `pgrep -fl` on a broad pattern, and never print full command
lines.** Use `pgrep -f <narrow>` for PIDs only, or read the store's own active
records, which is what actually answers "who else is live" in this project.
Mistake 5. The machine-level memory note carrying the old, wrong advice has
been corrected in place.
